prerequisites: Programming, computer, and network knowledge from basic degree courses

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the services and management tools integrated into an operating system
Perform basic administration tasks of a multitasking operating system in a network environment
Install and configure applications and services in a computer system (physical or in the cloud) to achieve the required system functionality

syllabus_topics: Concepts of systems administration. Installation of Linux and Windows operating systems. Linux administrative tools. Windows administration console.
System boot and shutdown. Boot sequence. Linux service startup and shutdown scripts: runlevels, upstart, systemd. Troubleshooting Linux and Windows boot issues.
Disks and file systems: ext3-4, NTFS. Journals. Disk administration. Partitioning. Logical volumes. Disk arrays. Partition managers. Quotas. Other storage devices.
Linux and Windows directory structure. Software installation and update. Linux packages. System update. Kernel modules. Windows drivers.
Backups. Backup tools. Simple backup. Multi-level backup.
User management and administration. Authentication systems
User accounts. Creation, deletion, changing properties of local users.
Local user authentication. Local groups. Resource access permissions.
Windows networks. Active Directory. Domains. Organizational units.
Network file systems: NFS and Samba/CIFS. Network backup.
Windows and Linux network services (DNS, WINS, DHCP, mail, SSH, Terminal Server, etc.)
Server migrations and basic virtualization concepts
Migration of a physical server to a virtual server
Installation of operating systems and database applications.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices / field / computer lab / language lab

assessment_methods.method: Formative and continuous evaluation of practical work
Final evaluation of practical work (product, report, oral presentation)
Theoretical exam (if average theoretical assignment grade is below 7)

assessment_rules: The final grade depends on theoretical assignment performance. If the average of theoretical assignments is 7 or higher, the final grade is calculated as (0.5 × Practical Grade) + (0.5 × Average Theoretical Assignments Grade). If the average of theoretical assignments is below 7, a theoretical exam is required, and the final grade is (0.5 × Practical Grade) + (0.35 × Average Theoretical Assignments Grade) + (0.15 × Theoretical Exam Grade). Both theoretical and practical parts must be passed separately. The professor may require a videoconference to verify knowledge.
